### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results. | # | Step | What to Do | Tips | |---|------|------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | • Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.).
• Set a budget (CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, case, PSU, peripherals). | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to check compatibility and prices. | | 2 | **Gather Components** | • CPU (Intel/AMD)
• Motherboard (socket, chipset, form‑factor)
• RAM (DDR4/DDR5, speed, capacity)
• GPU (if not integrated)
• Storage (SSD/HDD, NVMe or SATA)
• Power Supply Unit (PSU, wattage, 80+ rating)
• Case (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX, size, airflow)
• Cooling (stock cooler, aftermarket air cooler, AIO liquid cooler)
• Operating System (Windows, Linux, etc.) | Check compatibility: CPU socket vs motherboard, RAM type, GPU clearance, PSU connectors. | | 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | • Clean, flat, static‑free surface.
• Anti‑static wrist strap (recommended).
• Screwdrivers (Phillips #0, #1). | Avoid carpet; use a static mat if possible. | | 4 | **Install the CPU** | 1. Open the motherboard’s CPU socket latch.
2. Align the CPU (gold triangle) with the socket corner.
3. Gently place it, then lock the latch. | Don’t force; the socket will guide. | | 5 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | • If cooler doesn’t have pre‑applied paste, apply a pea‑size amount on the CPU center.
• Mount the cooler according to its instructions. | For AIO coolers, attach the pump to the motherboard header. | | 6 | **Insert RAM** | • Open the RAM slots’ clips.
• Align the notch on the RAM stick with the slot key.
• Push firmly until the clips click. | Install in pairs for dual‑channel (e.g., slot 1 & 3). | | 7 | **Mount the Motherboard in the Case** | 1. Place standoffs in the case matching the motherboard holes.
2. Align the motherboard with the I/O shield.
3. Secure with screws. | Double‑check that all standoffs are correctly positioned. | | 8 | **Install Storage** | • For NVMe SSD: slide into the M.2 slot, screw down.
• For SATA SSD/HDD: mount in drive bay, connect SATA data cable to motherboard, SATA power cable from PSU. | Label cables if you have many drives. | | 9 | **Install GPU** | 1. Remove the appropriate expansion slot covers on the case.
2. Insert GPU into the top PCI‑e x16 slot.
3. Secure with screws.
4. Connect required PCI‑e power cables from PSU. | Ensure the GPU is fully seated; it should click into place. | |10 | **Connect Power Cables** | • 24‑pin ATX to motherboard.
• 8‑pin (or 4‑pin) CPU power.
• PCI‑e power to GPU.
• SATA power to drives.
• Front panel connectors (USB, audio, power button). | Refer to the motherboard manual for exact pin layout. | |11 | **Cable Management** | • Route cables neatly behind the motherboard tray.
• Use zip ties or Velcro straps.
• Keep airflow unobstructed. | Good cable management improves airflow and makes future upgrades easier. | |12 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | 1. Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse.
2. Power on.
3. Enter BIOS (usually Delete or F2).
4. Verify CPU, RAM, storage detected.
5. Set boot priority to your OS installation media.
6. Save & exit. | Update BIOS if needed (check motherboard website). | |13 | **Install Operating System** | • Insert USB/DVD with OS installer.
• Follow on‑screen prompts to format/install.
• Install drivers (chipset, GPU, Wi‑Fi). | Use the latest drivers from manufacturer sites. | |14 | **Install Software & Updates** | • Windows Update, antivirus, productivity tools.
• Game launchers, video editors, etc. | Keep system updated for security and performance. | |15 | **Test & Benchmark** | • Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, FurMark).
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner).
• Check stability. | If temperatures are high, improve cable routing or add fans. | | 16 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | • Keep dust‑free, clean fans.
• Update drivers regularly.
• Monitor temperatures and performance. | Periodic cleaning (every 3–6 months) keeps longevity. | --- #### Quick Checklist - [ ] CPU & cooler installed - [ ] RAM seated - [ ] Motherboard mounted - [ ] PSU connected - [ ] GPU installed - [ ] Storage connected - [ ] All cables routed - [ ] BIOS detects all components - [ ] OS installed - [ ] Drivers updated - [ ] System stable --- #### Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Issue | Likely Cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | PC won’t power on | PSU not connected or switched off | Check PSU switch, verify all power cables | | GPU not recognized | Not seated properly or missing power cable | Re‑insert GPU, connect PCI‑e power | | Overheating | Poor airflow, inadequate cooling | Add case fans, improve cable management | | BIOS not detecting RAM | Wrong slot or incompatible RAM | Try different slots, check DDR version | | Blue screen after OS install | Driver conflict | Update or roll back drivers | --- #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & compatibility checker. - **YouTube** – “How to build a PC” series (e.g., Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents). - **Manufacturer manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and case manuals. - **Reddit r/buildapc** – Community help & advice. Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know which step and I’ll help troubleshoot.
message.reasoning: User asks: "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions. We can provide a step-by-step guide. No function call needed.
